October 25, 2026

Obama attacks Trump and Hegseth over Iran war and oil prices

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas

In rally remarks, Barack Obama said the war with Iran began after Donald Trump withdrew from the nuclear agreement that had constrained Iran's program without military action. He said that seven months into the conflict, US allies and bases have been attacked, Americans have been killed and hundreds wounded, missile stocks have been drawn down, and Iran now holds effective veto power over the Strait of Hormuz, driving up the price of oil, diesel and other goods. He also mocked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, saying he is focused on the jaw lines and testosterone levels of troops and on live-streaming executions.

Obama draws large crowds as Republicans warn of collapse nine days from midterms

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Barack Obama campaigned in Michigan and Ohio to packed venues, contrasting with Donald Trump's rally in Georgia for Mike Collins against John Ossoff. Trump claimed Obama's Michigan event was empty and spent the night posting on Truth Social calling Obama grossly incompetent and accusing him of paying Iran billions. Republican operatives quoted afterward said the bottom is falling out of the party's position, pointing to Trump's closing message on gas prices, in which he said his side is making a fortune while voters suffer at the pump. Obama also mocked Trump for focusing on White House renovations, a ballroom, a helicopter pad and gold decor.

Musk says he cut Starlink access for Ukrainian drone strikes as Russia praises him

tags: war, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

Elon Musk said that using Starlink for offensive drone strikes has never been permitted and that the Ukrainian military violated the terms of service, adding that the loophole was closed last week. The shutdown was followed by Ukrainian civilian deaths, and Musk had initially attributed the decision to the White House. Kirill Dmitriev, an envoy for Vladimir Putin, publicly praised Musk as a peacemaker, after a Trump envoy had described Putin as a humanitarian.

Trump administration exempts 202 facilities from Clean Air Act rules

tags: health, climate, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

An investigation found that since taking office Donald Trump has exempted 202 industrial facilities across 39 states and Puerto Rico from Clean Air Act regulations that were due to take effect. The facilities include chemical manufacturers, copper smelters, coal-burning power plants, sterilizers and steel-related plants, concentrated in the South and East. An estimated 3.3 million people live within three miles of at least one of the exempted sites, which emit gases linked to cancer.

Musk spends $446 million on 2026 midterms, most by any single donor

tags: politics, elections
sources: @carolinegleich

New federal filings show Elon Musk has contributed about $446 million of his own money to the 2026 midterm elections, the largest sum from a single donor in modern American history. Over the past two decades his companies have received at least $38 billion in government contracts, loans, subsidies and tax credits. Much of the spending funds online advertising attacking Democratic Senate candidates over transgender issues, and fact checkers found some ads misrepresent the candidates' voting records.

Lula defeats Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazilian presidential runoff

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

Brazil's electoral authority reported that President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won re-election in the October 25 runoff, defeating right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party. The result gives Lula, of the Workers' Party, a fourth non-consecutive term, extending the presidency he resumed in 2023 after defeating Jair Bolsonaro in 2022. The outcome was not widely predicted after the first round of voting. Jair Bolsonaro, the defeated candidate's father, is imprisoned in Brazil.

Serbia's ruling party loses snap election to student-backed list

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Serbian Prime Minister Aleksandar Vucic announced that his majority party has lost parliamentary elections to candidates backed by the country's student protest movement. Vucic, in power for more than a decade, had called the snap election in an attempt to consolidate power. The student-backed list will hold a parliamentary majority, with the ruling party reduced to roughly 104 to 105 seats.

Pentagon launches Operation Fortress to make bases self-sufficient for 90 days

tags: defence, war
sources: @aaronparnas

The Pentagon has begun a program to prepare US military bases to operate for at least 90 days without outside support. The initiative, called Operation Fortress, is intended for scenarios in which a major war cripples power grids, disrupts supply chains and threatens critical infrastructure, and would move bases off standard civilian infrastructure. The plans are described as long-term contingency planning rather than a response to any immediate conflict.

Trump claims $825 million conservation write-off on Florida golf course

tags: politics, legal, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

According to Forbes, Donald Trump took in roughly $1.4 billion from crypto in 2025 and more than $200 million from real estate, facing a projected tax bill above $500 million. His company donated development rights at his Jupiter, Florida golf course to a land trust on the argument that the course is natural habitat worth protecting, while continuing to operate the club, producing a write-off of $825 million. It is the fifth such transaction since 2005, and he sued the IRS a month after the Jupiter deal. An audit agreement struck with his former personal criminal defense attorney, now Attorney General, limits IRS action.

Fannie Mae pushes mortgage rate relief to 2028 as housing market stalls

tags: markets, economy
sources: @ericmoutsos

Fannie Mae revised its forecast to project mortgage rates of about 7.5% through the end of 2027, up from a prior estimate of 6.7% for next year, and said rates will not come down until 2028. Home builder sentiment fell to 29, the lowest reading since June 2012, with 43% of builders cutting prices last month and 65% offering incentives. Existing home sales have sat at 30-year lows for four straight years, and sellers now outnumber buyers by 63%, the widest gap recorded. In Florida, Lee County has more than 24,000 homes listed, a record, and the state has over two million vacant homes.

IUCN finds 96% of shallow coral reef ecosystems critically endangered

tags: climate, environment
sources: @groundnews

A global assessment by the International Union for Conservation of Nature found that 96% of the world's shallow-water coral reef ecosystems are critically endangered and could collapse by 2075, driven by rising ocean temperatures and marine heat waves. The assessment covered reefs across 127 tropical and subtropical regions, including the Great Barrier Reef, the Coral Triangle and the Red Sea, which together support a quarter of marine species and underpin food supplies, tourism and coastal protection. Pollution and overfishing also contribute to decline. Scientists said cutting greenhouse gas emissions, protecting marine habitats and restoring damaged reefs could improve survival prospects.

New York archdiocese to pay more than $800 million to settle 1,300 abuse claims

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews

The Archdiocese of New York has reached an $800 million settlement with approximately 1,300 people who accused Catholic clergy of sexual abuse, the second-largest such settlement involving a US Catholic archdiocese. Archbishop Ronald Hicks confirmed the agreement, which remains pending signatures expected in November and would conclude more than seven years of litigation. It follows a 2024 Los Angeles settlement of $880 million with 1,000 survivors. New York's 2019 Child Victims Act allowed many survivors to bring previously time-barred claims.

Documentary alleges Lindsey Graham paid male escorts, including a 17-year-old

tags: politics, media
sources: @groundnews

A documentary from The Young Turks and Swamp Watch Studios, titled "The CLOSETocracy," alleges that the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham paid three male escorts for sex, one of whom says he was 17 at the time. A participant identified as Kelvin alleges Graham paid him $120 for sex in Arizona in 2001. The film presents the accounts alongside Graham's record of opposing LGBTQ+ rights, including same-sex marriage. Graham, who died in July at 71, denied being gay during his lifetime, and the allegations have not been independently verified.

Two female sailors advance through BUD/S under Hegseth

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Two female sailors are being put through the Navy SEAL training pipeline, BUD/S, with one reportedly given a third attempt and a personal trainer, described as unprecedented in the Navy's history. The accommodation has drawn criticism within the SEAL community, which is credited with helping secure Pete Hegseth's appointment as Secretary of Defense. Critics argue the same decision under a previous administration would have provoked an outcry.

Trump invokes Nicki Minaj in midterm closing message amid press secretary speculation

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Reports circulated that the White House is considering Nicki Minaj for the role of press secretary, characterised as almost certainly not serious. At a rally forming part of his closing midterm message, Donald Trump made remarks about Minaj's appearance. The comments came as prices remain high and the administration's approval ratings stay low.
